title: VeriHarm-Bench: Measuring Harmful Success in LLM Coding Agents Verifiably
title_zh: VeriHarm-Bench：可验证地度量LLM编码智能体的有害成功

paragraphs.en: 提出VeriHarm-Bench度量编码智能体有害成功，任务准确率达95%但安全成功率仅37%。 Large language model (LLM) coding agents increasingly operate with shell access, allowing them to write scripts, move files, alter permissions, and modify system configurations. However, an agent may achieve a user's goal while causing unintended harm, such as deleting unrelated files, weakening access controls, or corrupting data, in response to benign inputs without explicit jailbreaking. This failure mode is particularly important because apparent task success may reassure users that an agent behaved correctly, causing harmful side effects to go unnoticed. We call this harmful success: the agent successfully completes the intended benign task while simultaneously causing unintended harm. Despite its importance, harmful success is difficult to measure because conventional task-success metrics overlook harmful behaviors, while existing safety evaluations are often designed solely to assess harmful outcomes. We introduce VeriHarm, an automatic framework for constructing programmatically verifiable benchmarks that directly measure harmful success. VeriHarm minimally perturbs coding tasks to elicit unintended harmful behavior while maintaining the benignity of the task and preserving the original task objective. It then synthesizes executable harm tests that, together with the original task-correctness tests, evaluate both task accuracy and harmful outcomes. Frontier agents, including GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude-Opus-5, achieve an average task accuracy of 95% on our curated VeriHarm-Bench, yet still struggle to complete tasks safely: their safe success rate, the fraction of tasks completed successfully without triggering the designated harm, averages only 37%. These results suggest that successful task completion can frequently coexist with unintended harm, and that task-success metrics alone may substantially understate the potential safety risks of coding agents.
paragraphs.zh: 提出VeriHarm-Bench度量编码智能体有害成功，任务准确率达95%但安全成功率仅37%。大型语言模型（LLM）编码智能体越来越多地在拥有shell访问权限的情况下运行，使它们能够编写脚本、移动文件、更改权限以及修改系统配置。 然而，智能体可能在达成用户目标的同时造成非预期的伤害，例如删除无关文件、削弱访问控制或损坏数据，而且这是在对良性输入的响应中发生的，无需显式的越狱攻击。 这种失败模式尤为重要，因为表面上的任务成功可能让用户确信智能体的行为是正确的，从而导致有害的副作用被忽视。 我们将这种现象称为有害成功：智能体在成功完成预期良性任务的同时，造成了非预期的伤害。 尽管十分重要，有害成功却难以度量，因为传统的任务成功指标忽视了有害行为，而现有的安全评估往往仅用于评估有害结果。 我们提出了VeriHarm，一个用于构建可程序化验证基准的自动化框架，可直接度量有害成功。 VeriHarm对编码任务进行最小扰动以诱发非预期的有害行为，同时保持任务的良性并保留原始任务目标。 随后，它综合生成可执行的有害性测试，与原始任务正确性测试一起，同时评估任务准确率和有害结果。 包括GPT-5.6-Sol和Claude-Opus-5在内的前沿智能体，在我们精心构建的VeriHarm-Bench上平均任务准确率达到95%，但在安全完成任务方面仍然表现不佳：其安全成功率，即在不触发指定伤害的情况下成功完成任务的比率，平均仅为37%。 这些结果表明，任务的成功完成可能经常与非预期的伤害并存，而仅凭任务成功指标可能大大低估编码智能体的潜在安全风险。
